_id: clk002 -- refLegacyHTable. clock rung: the OSCILLATOR CLASS axis. One clock choice against golden_baseline.json; every other leaf is inherited through _extends, so the delta in the result is attributable to the oscillator alone. SPACE segment = cfg.asset.clockType, the spacecraft receiver clock, whose bias/drift are EKF states and whose process noise Q is taken from the SAME models.clocks.ClockModel as the truth (filter.ReverseGNSSEKF:1498) -- truth and filter are matched by construction, so a space rung asks 'how good must the on-board oscillator be', not 'what does a Q mismatch cost'. GROUND segment = cfg.clock.tower.{clockType,deterministic}, which finalizeConfig maps onto every cfg.towers(k) (a JSON 'towers' key cannot be used: cfg.towers is a struct array, so deepMergeConfig would REPLACE it and drop every site's lat/lon/alt). Tower clocks are NOT EKF states here -- clock.mode is 'spacecraftReceiverClockOnly' and clock.gauge.mode is 'externalTowerCorrections', so a tower oscillator is chased by the broadcast product and only its UNCORRECTED residual reaches the measurement.
_delta: REWRITTEN 2026-08-10. This rung used to set clock.templateSource = 'legacy', switching a whole second h-coefficient table. That table is gone: there is now ONE table, Winkel (2003) Table 2.1, in ConfigFactory.oscillatorCatalog_. The rung's QUESTION survives -- 'what was the frozen goldens' optimistic clock table worth?' -- and is now asked the honest way, by overriding the two coefficients sets that actually differed, as DATA, through clock.customOscillators. The gap clk002 - clk001 still measures exactly what it always did.
_whatWasLegacy: The old 'legacy' table was not a source, it was the project's original optimistic numbers. Only two of its four classes ever differed from the sourced table: CESIUM1 (h0 = 1e-26 -- an idealised maser, ~7 orders below a real caesium beam, against Winkel's Cesium1 h0 = 1e-19) and OCXO (hMinus2 = 2e-29 against Winkel's OCXO2 2.51e-22). TCXO and RUBIDIUM were byte-identical in both tables despite comments claiming they were 'aligned to JOW Table 2.1', which is why any past rung sweeping templateSource on those two measured nothing at all. The two overrides below reproduce the legacy numbers exactly.
_trap: TRAP the ground rungs exist to avoid: the ground clock TYPE is INERT while cfg.clock.tower.deterministic is true. A deterministic ClockModel returns identically zero bias (ClockModel.m:204/294), so no h-coefficient is ever read and TowerClockCorrectionProvider sees towerClkTruth = 0 for every oscillator class. VERIFIED in MATLAB on 2026-08-09: OCXO deterministic gives |b|max = 0 m over a 3600 s free run; the same OCXO stochastic gives 3.6e3 m. NOTE the masterConfig DEFAULT flipped to deterministic = false on 2026-08-10, so this rung now opts back OUT of the running ground oscillator ON PURPOSE, to hold the ground segment fixed while the space clock table is varied. The OCXO override below is therefore inert HERE by construction; it is written out so the rung states the full legacy table rather than half of it.
_mechanism: Mechanism the ground rungs actually exercise: clocks.tower.product.mode = 'truthHistoryProductNoisy' rebroadcasts the tower clock every updateInterval_s = 30 s with latency_s = 5 s, and predicts forward linearly from the TRUTH bias and drift at the product epoch (TowerClockCorrectionProvider.m:98-120). So the free-running wander is almost entirely corrected; what survives is the wander the linear prediction cannot follow over an age of 5 to 34 s -- and, since 2026-08-10, that surviving wander is CHARGED TO R by TowerClockCorrectionProvider.extrapolationWanderVar_ instead of being omitted from it. The non-obvious result this axis produced: the caesium beam LOSES to rubidium on the ground, because Winkel's Cesium1 is white-FM dominated (h0 = 1e-19) three orders above rubidium's, and its superior long-term stability never gets a chance to matter inside a 30 s product interval.
_combination: space = CESIUM1 (legacy coefficients)  |  ground = OCXO (deterministic, zero truth bias)  |  table = single, with the two legacy overrides below
_reportNote: compileTex 'auto' rather than the golden's 'require': a ladder rung's deliverable is its .mat, and a pdflatex hiccup must not throw away a finished run. ReportRunner only escalates a failed compile to an error under 'require'.
_monteCarloNote: monteCarlo.enable is FALSE on this axis, unlike golden_baseline.json and the feat/freq/ISL rungs, which inherit its 12 seeds x 900 s. MEASURED on clk001: the 3600 s arc takes ~7 min and the Monte-Carlo block another ~24 min, so it is roughly 3.5x the cost of the rung itself and would have made a 13-rung sweep ~6.5 h instead of ~1.5 h. What is given up is ONLY the pooled NIS/NEES consistency band appended to the .out log; the headline position, clock and attitude errors this axis compares come from the 3600 s arc and are unaffected. CONSEQUENCE for anyone reading these rungs: a clock rung states WHAT the error is, not whether the filter's covariance is statistically consistent at that setting. If a combination looks anomalous, re-run that one rung with monteCarlo.enable true before drawing a covariance conclusion from it.
